title: Learned anomaly search identifies three previously unlisted gravitational-lens candidates
summary: A learned image-representation and human-feedback anomaly search prioritized unusual sources in nearly four million galaxy images. The study identified three gravitational-lens candidates absent from the catalogs it cross-matched, alongside five previously listed lens systems. These are image-based candidates rather than newly confirmed lenses; spectroscopy and more reliable redshift information are needed to establish their physical nature.
ai_technology: EfficientNetB0 image representations; isolation forest; active learning with human feedback
organization: University of the Western Cape; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory; University of Manchester; University of Toronto; National Centre for Nuclear Research

evidence.tested: Visual inspection of learned-ranked DECaLS sources yielded three previously unlisted candidates, source labelsL6–L8. The source distinguishes one known confirmed lens and four known lens candidates from these three newly proposed objects.
evidence.unknown: The three objects are suspected lenses based on image morphology, not spectroscopically confirmed systems. Source photometric redshifts are unreliable for lens interpretation, and chance alignments remain possible. The broader 1635 anomaly count includes known objects and merger candidates and is not a count of newly established physical discoveries. This record dates the fully read March 29,2024 arXiv version; an earlier September 15,2023 version exists, with no absolute earliest-priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained EfficientNetB0 network supplies learned image representations. Isolation forest and active learning incorporating human interest scores prioritize objects for visual examination, leading to the specific three new lens-candidate proposals.

source_review.scope: Full relevant primary arXiv v2 image/model Methods, candidate-specific Table3 and lens interpretation limitations; exact version history and current journal publication-status metadata.
